Definition: a head of grain (as cut off)
BiblicalUsage: Meliy lah is the head of grain, the ear of wheat as it is cut off. Deuteronomy 23:25 lets a man pluck the ears with his hand as he walks through his neighbour's standing corn, but not put a sickle to it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the law is generous and firm at once: a hungry man may eat, but the harvest still belongs to its owner.
